claims.text: A tungsten-based refractory high-entropy alloy coating can serve as the load-bearing component of a wide-temperature self-lubricating material.
A multilayer or graded tungsten-based RHEA coating with a self-lubricating top layer will maintain low friction from room temperature to at least 600 °C.
The proposed multilayer coating will maintain low wear from room temperature to at least 600 °C.
Adding the self-lubricating top layer will not compromise the coating's mechanical strength.
The initial sputtered tungsten-based RHEA sublayer has a nanocrystalline BCC-type microstructure.
Controlled magnetron sputtering can deposit a suitable self-lubricating lamellar or oxide-forming top layer on the tungsten-based RHEA.
Tailored annealing after deposition will promote stable interfacial bonding between the top layer and the RHEA.
The treatment will form a stable, low-shear-strength top layer.
A high-strength RHEA underlayer will preserve the multilayer coating's load-bearing capacity.
The RHEA sublayer retains mechanical integrity under extreme high-temperature conditions.
The RHEA sublayer's high-temperature mechanical integrity results from its high melting temperature.
The RHEA sublayer's strong BCC framework is responsible for retaining mechanical integrity.
The engineered top layer forms lubricious films and oxides during service.
The top-layer films and oxides reduce friction across a broad temperature range.
The multilayer coating will outperform a single-phase RHEA or conventional coating at elevated temperatures.
A single-layer tungsten-based RHEA coating may exhibit increasing friction and wear above 300 °C.
Above 600 °C or under aggressive high-load or chemically reactive conditions, degradation of the top layer may reduce its lubrication effect.
The exact upper service temperature and long-term structural stability of the multilayer system are uncertain.
